newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says insurance business too small.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says insurance business too small.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG chairman Rolf Breuer said on Wednesday he considered the current level of the bank's insurance activities to be too small.
Breuer told the interim results news conference he was very satisfied with the bank's insurance activities in Germany, Italy and Spain, but added:
"It must be said that the business is relatively modest. As a stand-alone this is a very pleasant business. But it is too small compared with the size of our banking activities.

Breuer however said the bank was not looking at acquisitions in the insurance area because it was already well positioned in asset management, a related field which was growing in importance as a source of private pension provision.

"We fell very well equipped. We are already among Europe's top asset managers," Breuer said. He added Deutsche was now aiming to focus its asset management services on clients seeking to provide for their own pension.
"That is my strategic goal. We don't want to enter into the risk part (of insurance)".
